- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 10–14 day horizons; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture continuation; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias if sentiment remains bullish.
- If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often misreads trend; apply downward correction in next 5–7 days, especially if price drops >2%.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–5 days); if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment direction within 3–5 days.
